Re: Appeal of denial of prior authorization for partial knee replacement  
CPT 27446

Dear Aetna Appeals Department:

I appeal the denial of prior authorization for partial knee replacement, CPT 27446. The stated reason for denial is that the submitted imaging does not support medical necessity. The clinical records directly document the radiographic severity and the other medical-necessity factors relevant to this procedure.

The applicable publicly available Aetna policy is Clinical Policy Bulletin 0660, Knee Arthroplasty. The policy states:

“Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty using Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved devices is considered medically necessary for members with advanced osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee affecting only a single compartment (medial, lateral or patellofemoral), and who meet the following criteria.”

“Pain and functional disability that interferes with ADLs due to osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint.”

“Limited range of motion, crepitus, or effusion or swelling of knee joint on physical examination.”

“Radiographic evidence of moderate/severe osteoarthritis (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) affecting only a single (medial, lateral or patellofemoral) compartment of the knee joint.”

The submitted records satisfy these requirements:

1. Imaging and single-compartment disease  
The June 2, 2026 MRI documents full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition. The imaging is graded Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially. This is severe osteoarthritis involving the medial compartment and directly satisfies the policy’s radiographic requirement for moderate or severe disease, specifically grade 3 or 4, affecting one compartment.

2. Pain and functional disability  
The patient has experienced 12 months of progressive knee pain that has not been relieved by rest. The pain prevents climbing stairs without assistance and causes the patient to awaken three to four times nightly. These limitations demonstrate substantial interference with activities of daily living.

3. Examination findings  
The examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. These findings support the presence of clinically significant knee pathology and functional impairment.

4. Failure of conservative treatment  
The patient completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including quadriceps strengthening and range-of-motion work, from March 9, 2026, through June 29, 2026, with 16 visits documented in the physical therapy discharge note. The patient also used NSAIDs for eight months without adequate relief. A corticosteroid injection on April 8, 2026, produced only three weeks of partial relief. The records therefore document prolonged unsuccessful nonsurgical treatment, including formal supervised physical therapy, medication, and injection treatment.

The policy also states:

“Member must have intact, stable ligaments, in particular the anterior cruciate ligament.”

“Patient’s knee arc of motion (full extension to full flexion) is not limited to 90 degrees or less.”

The records provided with this appeal document range of motion limited by pain, but do not state the precise knee arc in degrees or expressly document ligament stability. Please obtain and consider the surgeon’s supplemental statement confirming the ligament findings and exact range of motion: [insert surgeon’s statement regarding ligament stability and knee arc of motion].

The policy further states:

“Member has none of the following contraindications to unicompartmental knee arthroplasty: Previous proximal tibial osteotomy or distal femoral osteotomy; or Tibial or femoral shaft deformity; or Radiographic evidence of medial or lateral subluxation; or Flexion contracture greater than 15 degrees; or Varus deformity greater than 15 degrees (medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty) or a valgus deformity greater than 20 degrees (lateral unicompartmental knee arthroplasty); or Inflammatory or crystalline arthropathy; or Subchondral bone loss due to large subchondral cysts or extensive focal osteonecrosis.”

The submitted summary does not report these contraindications. The surgeon should provide a specific statement addressing each one: [insert surgeon’s confirmation regarding the listed contraindications].

The patient also has no active infection, has no untreated substance-use condition, has a BMI of 29, and is a nonsmoker. The record should also include the date of the planned surgery and a statement addressing whether the April 8, 2026 corticosteroid injection occurred within 12 weeks of the planned arthroplasty: [insert planned surgery date and surgeon’s statement].

I request that Aetna overturn the denial and approve CPT 27446 based on the documented grade 4 medial-compartment disease, bone-on-bone cartilage loss, significant pain and functional impairment, and failure of extensive conservative treatment. If Aetna continues to deny the request, please provide the specific imaging findings considered insufficient, identify every criterion that Aetna contends has not been met, and provide the clinical review criteria and records relied upon in making the determination.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and notify me of the appeal decision in writing.

Sincerely,

Skyler Brooks
